messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: make test-bugs
parts:
Hi all,

The test-bugs target has changed a bit. The examples now run within
google tests. This allows us to record execution time to be displayed
through Jenkins. See:
http://d1m1s1b1.stat.columbia.edu:8080/job/Stan%20Model%20Tests/

There is also a test-models target that will run tests for the other
*.stan files in src/models/

The downside is that the unit tests are generated by hand. test-models
will indicate whether any Stan models are in src/models but don't have
associated tests. Once we have the chains object up and running, we
can get the automatic testing we've been planning. The performance
plugin for Jenkins tracks percentage of failed tests, so perhaps we
don't need to worry too much about "failures" of individual tests.






Daniel

On Tuesday, May 29, 2012 8:44:14 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: make test-bugs
parts:
On Tuesday, May 29, 2012 10:18:03 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Any ideas on how to run the models in parallel?

If you apply this patch:

diff --git a/make/tests b/make/tests
index d42df92..5a63cca 100644
--- a/make/tests
+++ b/make/tests
@@ -22,7 +22,7 @@ test-models: $(addsuffix $(EXE),$(MODEL_TESTS))
        @set -e;\
        $(foreach test,$(MODEL_TESTS), \
          echo '------------------------------------------------------------';\
-         $(addsuffix $(EXE),$(test)) --gtest_output="xml:$(test).xml";)
+         $(addsuffix $(EXE),$(test)) --gtest_output="xml:$(test).xml" & )
 ifneq ($(MISSING_MODEL_TESTS),)
        @echo
        @echo '-------------------- Missing $(words $(MISSING_MODEL_TESTS)) tests --------------------'


then the loop backgrounds the execution of the model and goes onto the next test. This is not ideal because

-- It does not respect the -j argument, so it ties up the machine
-- For me, it launches 16 threads across 8 virtual cores at about 50% CPU each, so not super-efficient
-- It makes a mess out of the output that gets piped to the shell

But, it is better than doing it serial particularly since these models take more than 25 minutes of CPU time

-- vol1/oxford
-- vol1/lsat
-- vol2/t_df/simt4
-- vol1/inhalers

Ben

If we did want to run them in parallel, I think the correct thing to
do is for test-models to depend on a bunch of phony targets. There
should be one phony target per test. Each phony target would depend on
the test it is responsible for running. The phony target's action
should be to run the test.

Unfortunately, that would still cause the output to get mangled, but
it would do what you want. Want to give it a try? Maybe give it a
different target -- like test-models-parallel?



Daniel
